summary: Wu Hung is an archaeologist and Sinologist who studied at Harvard University from ~1980 to 1987. He became a professor at the University of Chicago around 1994 and held a post at the Smart Museum of Art around 1999.
Wulstan Fletcher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xianda works in Buddhist studies, earning a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016). Xianda studied under Toshiichi Endo and K. L. Dhammajoti.

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tsinghua University (1930–1934) and the University of Göttingen (1935–1941). He held posts at Göttingen (1937) and Peking University (1946; Life Professor 1980).

Xiaoling Wu worked in Sinology and Indology. He was a lecturer and research scholar at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1947), and held posts at Peking University (~1949–1953), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Peking University (~1954–1958). He served as a researcher (研究員) at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from ~1978 to 2010.

Xinru Liu works in Indology, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), she taught at The College of New Jersey (~1999) and held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2010).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor (副教授) at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011 and a Research Associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017).

Y. Karunadasa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral research under David Friedman at SOAS, University of London (~1960–1963). He served as Director at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University under Gregory Schopen, David Shulman, and others, later teaching in the Department of Indian Studies at the Hebrew University (attested 2000).
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies and Sinology and earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hojin (attested 2003) and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich by 1998.
Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the doctoral supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).
Yao Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (attested 2010).
